info.bio:
Mr. Bungle fue un grupo musical norteamericano formado el año 1985 en Eureka, California, con Mike Patton como vocalista. En sus comienzos, integró estilos musicales como el rock, heavy metal, funk y jazz, resultando en algo similar al funk metal. En sus posteriores trabajos, integraron estilos como el ska, swing y pop, entre otros estilos. La banda se disolvió el 2003.

Sus integrantes fundadores fueron Trevor Dunn en el bajo, Mike Patton en las voces, Trey Spruance en las guitarras y Jed Watts en la batería.

scenes.desc: Phish devuelven el rock alternativo a la radio y legitiman el regreso a la estética progresiva, sobre todo en la Costa Este: Blues Traveler, Motherhead Bug y Sulfur, Spin Doctors, Klezmatics, Cul De Sac (Ecim, China Gate) y Run On. El noise-punk-jazz de God Is My Co-pilot, Molecules, Love Child, Blowhole, Harry Pussy. Virginia como epicentro (Echolyn, Boud Deun, Rake, Dave Matthews Band). Solistas: Marc Ribot, Nicky Skopelitis, Buckethead, Loren Mazzacane, los zappianos Ant-Bee y Mike Keneally, Gary Lucas, Alan Licht, Bob Drake. En la Costa Oeste, Primus (Frizzle Fry), Mr Bungle, Amy Denio, Caveman Shoestore, Thessalonians. Internacional: Philharmonie, Xaal, Volapuk, Kevin Martin (God, Techno Animal, Ice, Bug). Y la Babel final: Bright, Meringue, Cerberus Shoal, Tin Hat Trio, Species Being.

podcast.title: Arrest for Murder (Early January 2023)
podcast.body: Fio Lendiel, also known as Milo Stone, was arrested in early January 2023 and charged with the murder of his girlfriend, Alex. Alex was last seen on December 6, 2023, and reported missing on December 12th after failing to board a scheduled trip to Hawaii. Her remains were later found in a park in Berkeley, California, and Lendiel's Toyota pickup was discovered in front of his house. "In early January 2023, he was arrested and charged with Alex's murder."

podcast.title: Masks, Jumpsuits, and Pseudonyms
podcast.body: Mr. Bungle, a group fronted by Mike Patton of Faith No More, is known for incorporating masks, jumpsuits, and pseudonyms into their image. "The group headed up by Mike Patton of Faith No More. They've been known to use masks and jumpsuits and pseudonyms too."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mike Patton's Original Band
podcast.body: Before joining Faith No More in January 1989, Mike Patton was the singer for his own group, Mr. Bungle. He had met Faith No More members in 1986. "Mike was in his own group called Mr. Bungle, and had met Faith No More sometime in 1986."

podcast.title: Post-Faith No More Band
podcast.body: Mr. Bungle was one of the musical groups that emerged from the individual pursuits of Faith No More members after their initial split. "There were post-faith no more bands like Imperial Teen and Mr. Bungle."

xref.title: Influences on Mask Concept
xref.body: Kiss was a major influence on Slipknot members, who admired the anonymity offered by makeup. Mr. Bungle, fronted by Mike Patton of Faith No More, also served as an influence, known for using masks, jumpsuits, and pseudonyms. "First, Kiss was a big influence on every member of Slipknot. They loved the anonymity that make up offered them. Another influence was the band Mr. Bungle, the group headed up by Mike Patton of Faith No More. They've been known to use masks and jumpsuits and pseudonyms too."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Members' Post-Breakup Projects
xref.body: Following the breakup, members pursued various endeavors: other bands like Imperial Teen and Mr. Bungle were formed, some made guest appearances and received production credits, and record labels were established. Drummer Mike Bordin worked with Ozzy Osborne for a period, and guitarist Jim Martin transitioned to growing 1,300-pound pumpkins professionally. "Drummer Mike Bowden went off to work with Ozzy Osborne for a while."

xref.title: Mike Patton Joins
xref.body: After Chuck Mosley's departure, the remaining members reconvened and approached Mike Patton, who was the singer for Mr. Bungle and had met Faith No More in 1986. Patton joined as lead singer by January 1989, and promptly wrote all the lyrics for their next album in two weeks. "After the Mosley Fiasco, he was approached to become the lead singer, and by January 1989, he was in."
